does: GET /accounts/{account_id}/tokens/verify（账户令牌；失败时再试 GET /user/tokens/verify 用户令牌）：token 是否有效、是否 active
GET /accounts/{account_id}/warp_connector?per_page=1：能否在这个账户读取 Mesh 节点
GET /accounts/{account_id}/teamnet/routes?per_page=1&is_deleted=false：能否在这个账户读取路由
does_not: 不创建、不修改、不删除任何东西
不能证明写权限：两个列表接口同时接受 Read 与 Write 权限
不读取 token 的权限清单（那需要额外的 API Tokens Read 权限）

how_to: Cloudflare 控制台 → 管理账户 → 账户 API 令牌（Account API Tokens）→ 创建令牌 → 自定义令牌（Cloudflare 要求第一个 API token 在控制台创建）。
权限只加两项，均为账户级：Cloudflare One Connectors · Edit/Write；Cloudflare One Networks · Edit/Write。
账户资源选择要部署 Mesh 的那个账户；不需要任何区域（zone）权限。
可选：设置客户端 IP 过滤为网关的出口 IP、设置到期时间。
创建后把 token 和账户 id（32 位十六进制，在账户首页右侧）填进面板；token 只写不读。

permissions.name: Cloudflare One Connectors Write
permissions.why: 创建、查询、删除 Mesh 节点（warp_connector），读取节点令牌

permissions.name: Cloudflare One Networks Write
permissions.why: 发布、列出、撤回 CIDR 路由（teamnet/routes）

does_not_prove: 隧道真的握手、流量真的经出口出去（端到端连通）
分流结果、DNS / IPv6 / WebRTC 不泄漏（「防泄露」页的验收要实际执行才算）
流媒体与 AI 服务的解锁（「解锁」页的探测）
远程接入的设备能从外网拨入
independent: 远程接入（开关与设备）是独立资源：保存拓扑、本引导的任何一步都不会打开、关闭或修改它；它的改动随网关的安装生效
Cloudflare Mesh 备路的部署和撤回在 Cloudflare 页，不在本引导里
proves: 在这次运行中实际安装的网关：meridian-host 的安装事务已提交——文件写入、接口与防火墙激活、服务启动，事务里的健康检查通过
在这次运行中实际下发的远端节点：装机脚本完成激活并写下清单，面板在同一登录里读回服务器上的记录，与装上去的内容一致（读回失败、不完整或不一致时这一步是「结果不明」，不算装好）
「已在服务器上（采纳）」：预检完整读到的服务器记录（网关是安装清单）已经是这份内容；没有重新执行，也没有重新检查健康——服务现在是否在运行没有核实

modes.full: 全隧道模式：手机的全部 IPv4/IPv6 流量和 DNS 都进隧道，由网关按家里局域网的规则处理：国内直连（从家里宽带出去）、境外走 Meridian 隧道、未分类拒绝，DNS 只能用网关。设备之间不能互访；面板只对家里局域网开放。
modes.home: 仅家网模式：只有家里局域网的地址和网关的 DNS 地址走隧道。手机访问公网仍走它当前的网络（蜂窝或别处的 Wi-Fi），不经过 Meridian，国内直连、境外走隧道和防泄漏规则都不作用于这部分流量；DNS 是否全部交给网关取决于手机系统，部分查询可能仍走当前网络的 DNS。要让 Meridian 接管全部流量请用全隧道模式。

body.shared_address: 网关按解析出的目的地址分流：两个指向不同目标的名字解析到同一个地址时，该地址按列表里更靠前的规则走。
upgrade_notes: 升级后，苹果和各系统的联网检测域名不再内置直连：没有规则指向直连时，它们和其它境外域名一样由默认组（或命中规则的目标）的解析器解析并走隧道。需要直连就启用「Apple 直连」模板或加一条直连规则。
升级后，靠前的规则优先于更长的后缀：以前解析器按“最长的名字”在规则之间选，现在按列表顺序第一条命中。结果因此改变的规则在「遮蔽」列标为“升级后变化”。
「未列名单的域名也问国内 DNS」默认关闭，规则和国内名单都不依赖它。

address_only: 所有 UDP，包括 QUIC（UDP 443 仍由「走隧道的流量拒绝 UDP 443」开关处理）
不在接管列表里的 TCP 端口
读不到名字的 TCP：没有 SNI、SNI 是地址、HTTP/2 明文前言、非 TLS/HTTP 协议、服务器先说话的协议、超时、畸形或超长
带 ECH 且明文名字是已知 ECH 公共名（默认 cloudflare-ech.com）的连接：真名字被加密，按目的地址
目的是本机、局域网、私有地址、远程接入地址池或已知 DoH 地址的连接（不接管）
接管之前已经建立的连接（只接管新连接的第一个 SYN）
by_name: 局域网和远程接入设备新建的 TCP 连接，目的端口在接管列表里（默认 80、443），并且客户端在 1 秒内发出了 TLS ClientHello 的 SNI 或 HTTP/1 的 Host：按名字在有序规则表里自上而下匹配（关键词规则按子串生效），再由目标自己的解析器重新解析后连接
costs: 带 ECH 扩展、明文名字不在公共名列表里的连接按明文名字判断：浏览器发的 GREASE ECH 时这就是真名字；真正启用 ECH 而提供方的公共名不在列表里时，会按那个公共名分流（通常落到默认组）
按名字判断的连接连接的是目标解析器给的地址，不是客户端自己解析到的地址
所有被接管的连接经过网关上的用户态转发，占用网关的 CPU 和内存，并增加约一个往返的建立时延（服务器先说话的协议多等 1 秒）
服务停止或崩溃时被接管的连接直接失败，不会回落到按地址的路径
中继被淘汰时，转发服务已建立的连接不会像转发流量那样被立即重置，而是留在原中继上直到结束；新连接按新的权重分配

body.ingest_rule: unlocked = 成功，not_unlocked = 失败；network_ok / unknown / failed 不是解锁结论，按 inconclusive 入库，既不降级也不恢复；not_applicable（检测方法不支持这个地址族，没有发出请求）不入库

reasons.discontinued: 平台已停止或并入别的服务，公开方法已过时
reasons.fake_login: 公开方法提交伪造的登录表单看错误码，本项目不提交任何登录请求
reasons.header_only: 判断依据在应答头或 Set-Cookie 里，探测不把应答头和 Cookie 交给分类器
reasons.needs_js: 公开方法要执行页面脚本，或从主机不固定的脚本里抓参数，放不进固定主机名单
reasons.needs_token: 公开方法要把账号、应用令牌、API key、播放器 policy key、设备标识或会话值当作请求参数，本项目不发送任何这类数据
reasons.not_https: 公开方法用明文 HTTP 或非 443 端口，探测只走 https/443
reasons.not_service: 不是流媒体或 AI 服务（地区识别、IP 信誉、CDN 位置、游戏、论坛），不是解锁判断；出口确认已经给出实际地区
reasons.transport: 公开方法降低 TLS 要求（允许旧式重协商）或直连写死的 IP 并改写 Host 头，探测不这样做
reasons.weak_signal: 只有不可靠的判断依据（写死的地区表、只看 HTTP 状态码（403 也可能是风控）、页面里的单个字样、第三方地理服务、只能读出地区而没有任何不可用标记）

+# IX is a dedicated line, not a host. Mesh is not in this list.

+#!/bin/bash
+# IX replacement is pre-provisioned. It takes traffic only after health failure or when IX_MODE=1.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+WEST_UDP="m02"
+WEST_WSS="m02w"
+EAST_IX="m00"
+EAST_WSS=""
+WEST_PEER_UDP="10.66.3.1"
+WEST_PEER_WSS="10.66.102.1"
+EAST_PEER_IX="10.66.1.2"
+EAST_PEER_WSS=""
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+state=/run/meridian/relay-failover
+mkdir -p /run/meridian
+
+alive() {
+  local iface="$1" peer="$2"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ping -I "$iface" -c 1 -W 2 -n "$peer" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+apply_east() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+}
+apply_west() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface" table 150
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface"
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  fi
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole "$LAN" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT4" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT6" metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace blackhole "$LAN6" metric 32767
+  fi
+}
+east_pref="$EAST_IX"
+[ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ] && east_pref="$EAST_WSS"
+west_pref="$WEST_UDP"
+[ -n "$west_pref" ] || west_pref="$WEST_WSS"
+cur_east="$east_pref"
+cur_west="$west_pref"
+east_bad=0
+west_bad=0
+last_switch=0
+while true; do
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  want_east="$EAST_IX"
+  if [ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ]; then
+    if alive "$EAST_WSS" "$EAST_PEER_WSS"; then want_east="$EAST_WSS"
+    elif alive "$EAST_IX" "$EAST_PEER_IX"; then want_east="$EAST_IX"
+    else want_east="$EAST_WSS"; fi
+  else
+    if alive "$EAST_IX" "$EAST_PEER_IX"; then want_east="$EAST_IX"
+    elif alive "$EAST_WSS" "$EAST_PEER_WSS"; then want_east="$EAST_WSS"
+    else want_east="$EAST_IX"; fi
+  fi
+  want_west="$WEST_UDP"
+  if alive "$WEST_UDP" "$WEST_PEER_UDP"; then want_west="$WEST_UDP"
+  elif alive "$WEST_WSS" "$WEST_PEER_WSS"; then want_west="$WEST_WSS"
+  fi
+  if [ "$want_east" != "$cur_east" ]; then
+    east_bad=$((east_bad+1))
+    if [ "$east_bad" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ] && [ $((now-last_switch)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" -o "$last_switch" -eq 0 ]; then
+      apply_east "$want_east"
+      cur_east="$want_east"
+      east_bad=0
+      last_switch=$now
+    fi
+  else
+    east_bad=0
+  fi
+  if [ "$want_west" != "$cur_west" ]; then
+    west_bad=$((west_bad+1))
+    if [ "$west_bad" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ]; then
+      apply_west "$want_west"
+      cur_west="$want_west"
+      west_bad=0
+    fi
+  else
+    west_bad=0
+  fi
+  sleep 5
+done
 
===== nodes/ali/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-563f4d9c
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m02 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m02"
+  "-i m02w -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m02w"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m00 m02 m02w; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit 'wstunnel-meridian.service'
+enable_unit meridian-failover.service
+systemctl restart meridian-failover.service
+echo meridian-up-complete

+# Transit node. Does not NAT client traffic and does not own the default route.

+  chain ingress_return_in {

+#!/bin/bash
+# IX replacement is pre-provisioned. It takes traffic only after health failure or when IX_MODE=1.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+WEST_UDP="m03"
+WEST_WSS=""
+EAST_IX="m01"
+EAST_WSS=""
+WEST_PEER_UDP="10.66.4.1"
+WEST_PEER_WSS=""
+EAST_PEER_IX="10.66.2.2"
+EAST_PEER_WSS=""
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+state=/run/meridian/relay-failover
+mkdir -p /run/meridian
+
+alive() {
+  local iface="$1" peer="$2"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ping -I "$iface" -c 1 -W 2 -n "$peer" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+apply_east() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+}
+apply_west() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface" table 150
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface"
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  fi
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole "$LAN" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT4" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT6" metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace blackhole "$LAN6" metric 32767
+  fi
+}
+east_pref="$EAST_IX"
+[ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ] && east_pref="$EAST_WSS"
+west_pref="$WEST_UDP"
+[ -n "$west_pref" ] || west_pref="$WEST_WSS"
+cur_east="$east_pref"
+cur_west="$west_pref"
+east_bad=0
+west_bad=0
+last_switch=0
+while true; do
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  want_east="$EAST_IX"
+  if [ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ]; then
+    if alive "$EAST_WSS" "$EAST_PEER_WSS"; then want_east="$EAST_WSS"
+    elif alive "$EAST_IX" "$EAST_PEER_IX"; then want_east="$EAST_IX"
+    else want_east="$EAST_WSS"; fi
+  else
+    if alive "$EAST_IX" "$EAST_PEER_IX"; then want_east="$EAST_IX"
+    elif alive "$EAST_WSS" "$EAST_PEER_WSS"; then want_east="$EAST_WSS"
+    else want_east="$EAST_IX"; fi
+  fi
+  want_west="$WEST_UDP"
+  if alive "$WEST_UDP" "$WEST_PEER_UDP"; then want_west="$WEST_UDP"
+  elif alive "$WEST_WSS" "$WEST_PEER_WSS"; then want_west="$WEST_WSS"
+  fi
+  if [ "$want_east" != "$cur_east" ]; then
+    east_bad=$((east_bad+1))
+    if [ "$east_bad" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ] && [ $((now-last_switch)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" -o "$last_switch" -eq 0 ]; then
+      apply_east "$want_east"
+      cur_east="$want_east"
+      east_bad=0
+      last_switch=$now
+    fi
+  else
+    east_bad=0
+  fi
+  if [ "$want_west" != "$cur_west" ]; then
+    west_bad=$((west_bad+1))
+    if [ "$west_bad" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ]; then
+      apply_west "$want_west"
+      cur_west="$want_west"
+      west_bad=0
+    fi
+  else
+    west_bad=0
+  fi
+  sleep 5
+done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-b0266c70
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m03 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m03"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.
+set -euo pipefail

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the

+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i
+  for i in "$@"; do
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.rp_filter=2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+  done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m01 m03; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-failover.service
+systemctl restart meridian-failover.service
+echo meridian-up-complete

+#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
+# exit dc1 public NAT. Tunnel ULA and the LAN prefix are translated here, not on the home gateway.
+table inet meridian
+delete table inet meridian
+table inet meridian {
+  chain group_dns {
+    type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat; policy accept;
+    iifname { "m05", "m12" } ip6 saddr { fd66:0:0:ff::10 } accept comment "region-group queries of the exits behind this node: not answered here"
+    iifname { "m05", "m12" } ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:d::2 comment "region-group resolver addresses: this exit's tunnel resolver"
+    iifname { "m05", "m12" } ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:d::2 comment "region-group resolver addresses: this exit's tunnel resolver"
+  }
+  chain hub_return_in {
+    type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
+    iifname "m12" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4d50 comment "arrived from the primary hub ix"
+    iifname "m05" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4d51 comment "arrived from the backup hub hk5"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "reply: back through the primary hub"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d51 meta mark set 0x4d51 comment "reply: back through the backup hub"
+  }
+  chain hub_return_out {
+    type route hook output priority mangle; policy accept;
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "local reply (resolver, ping): back through the primary hub"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d51 meta mark set 0x4d51 comment "local reply (resolver, ping): back through the backup hub"
+  }
+  chain exit_dns {
+    type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat; policy accept;
+    iifname { "m12", "m05" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:1 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:d::2 comment "this exit's resolver address, from either hub"
+    iifname { "m12", "m05" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:1 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:d::2 comment "this exit's resolver address, from either hub"
+  }
+  chain nested_guard {
+    type filter hook forward priority filter; policy accept;
+    ip saddr 10.66.200.16 oifname != "m19" counter drop comment "nested exit tw2: only into its tunnel, never this host's WAN"
+    ip6 saddr fd66:0:0:ff::10 oifname != "m19" counter drop
+  }
+  chain srcnat {
+    type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept;
+    oifname "eth0" ip saddr { 192.168.77.0/24, 10.66.200.0/24 } masquerade
+  }
+  chain drop_v6 {
+    type filter hook forward priority filter; policy accept;
+    oifname "eth0" meta nfproto ipv6 drop comment "no egress_v6; AAAA is filtered at DNS"
+  }
+}

===== nodes/dc1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-c289f476
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m05 -o m19"
+  "-i m19 -o m05"
+  "-i m12 -o m19"
+  "-i m19 -o m12"
+  "-i m05 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m05 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m12 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m12 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.
+set -euo pipefail
+del_rule() {
+  while "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; do :; done || true
+}
+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i
+  for i in "$@"; do
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.rp_filter=2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv6.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  done
+}

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='dc1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m05 m12 m19; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")

+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2

+  fi
+fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian external SOCKS exits health. Managed by Meridian (node manifest).
+# Health = a DNS query over TCP relayed by the redirector through the proxy
+# (TCP reachability through the proxy; no ICMP to the proxy, no credential here).
+set -u
+INTERVAL=10
+TIMEOUT=8
+mkdir -p /run/meridian/ext
+ext_probe() {
+  local addr="$1" port="$2" out
+  # 17-byte query: header (id 0x4d52, RD, one question), root name, NS, IN.
+  out=$(timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c 'exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/$0/$1" || exit 1; printf "\x00\x11\x4d\x52\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x01" >&3; head -c 4 <&3' "$addr" "$port" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
+  [ "${out:4:4}" = "4d52" ]
+}
+ext_check() {
+  local id="$1" svc="$2" health="$3" was now
+  was=$(cat "/run/meridian/ext/$id" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
+  if ext_probe "$svc" 5301 || ext_probe "$svc" 5302; then
+    now=up
+    ip addr replace "$health/32" dev lo
+  else
+    now=down
+    ip addr del "$health/32" dev lo 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  if [ "$now" != "$was" ]; then
+    echo "$now" > "/run/meridian/ext/$id"
+    if [ "$now" = up ]; then
+      echo "meridian-ext-health: $id up (TCP through its proxy answers); health address $health present"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-ext-health: $id down (no TCP answer through its proxy within ${TIMEOUT}s); health address $health removed, the hubs stop using it" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+}
+ext_all() {
+  ext_check 'my1' 10.66.201.14 10.66.202.14
+  :
+}
+keep_health=' 10.66.202.14 '
+for a in $(ip -o -4 addr show dev lo to 10.66.202.0/24 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}'); do case "$keep_health" in *" ${a%%/*} "*) ;; *) ip addr del "$a" dev lo 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac; done
+while true; do
+  ext_all
+  sleep "$INTERVAL"
+done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-4a5ba470
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m06 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m06 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m13 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m13 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.

+exit_id='dc2'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.

+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"

+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"

+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}

+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/

+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""

+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"

+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true

+delete table inet meridian
+table inet meridian {
+  chain group_dns {
+    type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat; policy accept;
+    iifname { "m07", "m14" } ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:f::2 comment "region-group resolver addresses: this exit's tunnel resolver"
+    iifname { "m07", "m14" } ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:f::2 comment "region-group resolver addresses: this exit's tunnel resolver"
+  }
+  chain hub_return_in {
+    type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
+    iifname "m14" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4d50 comment "arrived from the primary hub ix"
+    iifname "m07" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4d51 comment "arrived from the backup hub hk5"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "reply: back through the primary hub"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d51 meta mark set 0x4d51 comment "reply: back through the backup hub"
+  }
+  chain hub_return_out {
+    type route hook output priority mangle; policy accept;
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "local reply (resolver, ping): back through the primary hub"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d51 meta mark set 0x4d51 comment "local reply (resolver, ping): back through the backup hub"
+  }
+  chain exit_dns {
+    type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat; policy accept;
+    iifname { "m14", "m07" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:3 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:f::2 comment "this exit's resolver address, from either hub"
+    iifname { "m14", "m07" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:3 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:f::2 comment "this exit's resolver address, from either hub"
+  }

+    oifname "eth0" ip saddr { 192.168.77.0/24, 10.66.200.0/24 } masquerade

===== nodes/gb1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-4e89086b
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m07 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m07 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m14 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m14 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.

+  local i

+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv6.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  done
+}

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='gb1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m07 m14; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}

+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi

+#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
+# Meridian early-boot LAN guard. Loaded by meridian-guard.service before
+# forwarding can be enabled. Replaces only table inet meridian_guard.
+# LAN fail-closed guard. Independent of table inet meridian: it reads only
+# the fwmark and the output interface, so if classification is missing
+# every forwarded LAN packet is unmarked and dropped here.
+table inet meridian_guard
+delete table inet meridian_guard
+table inet meridian_guard {
+  chain forward {
+    type filter hook forward priority -200; policy accept;
+    iifname "eth0" meta l4proto { tcp, udp } th dport { 53, 853 } drop comment "DNS is answered locally, never forwarded"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x64 oifname "eth0" return comment "domestic: direct via ROS or LAN only"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x101-0x140 oifname { "m02", "m02w", "m03", "m04" } return comment "exit marks: WireGuard only"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x65 meta l4proto tcp reject with tcp reset comment "reject rules: TCP reset"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x65 reject with icmpx port-unreachable comment "reject rules: ICMP port unreachable"
+    iifname "eth0" counter drop comment "fail closed: unclassified or misrouted LAN traffic, v4 and v6"
+  }
+}

+# Meridian SmartDNS. Real answers, no fake-ip.
+# ECS is intentionally unset so the family prefix is not attached to queries.
+# Queries to an exit resolver leave from that exit's WAN, so DNS and the data path share a region.
+# A region group the hub switches resolves through its own data path (group mark, group
+# resolver address), so its DNS always reaches the member the hub currently uses.
+speed-check-mode none
+dualstack-ip-selection no
+cache-size 65536
+cache-persist no
+serve-expired yes
+rr-ttl-min 60
+bind [::]:53
+bind-tcp [::]:53
+# DoT certificate will not match the name the client dialed. Strict clients fail closed and fall back to port 53.
+# The certificate is global in SmartDNS (bind-cert-*); bind-tls takes no certificate options.
+bind-cert-file /etc/meridian/dns/cert.pem
+bind-cert-key-file /etc/meridian/dns/key.pem
+bind-tls [::]:853
+
+# AAAA: clients take IPv6 from the home router, not from this gateway (settings
+# clients_ipv6_via_gateway off): IPv6 to a tunnelled name would leave over the home line.
+# No AAAA (empty NOERROR, IPv6 hints dropped from HTTPS records) for any name except the
+# domestic sets and the rules allowed IPv6, which carry "-address -6".
+force-AAAA-SOA yes
+
+server-tls 192.0.2.53:853 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+server 192.0.2.53 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+server-tls 198.51.100.53:853 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+server 198.51.100.53 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+
+server fd66::54:1 -group g_dc1 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:2 -group g_dc2 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:3 -group g_gb1 -exclude-default-group

===== nodes/gw/usr/local/sbin/meridian-failover.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Relay sharing: every relay carries new connections at the weight the controller
+# (meridian path-step: measure, decide, record) sets from measured path quality; the
+# backup hub only while every relay is persistently below the usable floor.
+# Fallback when path-step is unavailable: equal weights over the relays that answer,
+# reachability only. Nothing answering: tables stay on tunnels (never the LAN NIC).
+set -u
+# relay sharing (compile.planShare); only share_apply changes the map and the relay tables at run time
+SH_NAME=('ali' 'ali2')
+SH_LEGS=('m02 m02w' 'm03')
+SH_PROBE=('10.66.1.2' '10.66.2.2')
+SH_TABLE=(111 112)
+SH_VALUE=(0x00010000 0x00020000)
+SH_BK_HUB='hk5'
+SH_BK_IFACE='m04'
+SH_BK_PROBE='10.66.5.2'
+SH_BK_TABLE='109'
+SH_BK_VALUE='0x00fe0000'
+SH_PRIMARY='ix'
+SH_IN='"eth0"'
+SH_HASH4='jhash ip saddr . ip daddr . th sport . th dport mod 1000 seed 0x4d52'
+SH_HASH6='jhash ip6 saddr . ip6 daddr . th sport . th dport mod 1000 seed 0x4d52'
+UP_STATE=/run/meridian/upstream
+SH_APPLIED=/run/meridian/pathq/applied
+share_index() {
+  local i
+  for ((i = 0; i < ${#SH_NAME[@]}; i++)); do
+    if [ "${SH_NAME[$i]}" = "$1" ]; then echo "$i"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+share_leg_ok() {
+  case "$2" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  case " ${SH_LEGS[$1]} " in *" $2 "*) return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+share_table_route() {
+  ip route replace default dev "$2" table "$1"
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$1"
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$2" table "$1"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$1"
+}
+# share_tables LEG_1 … LEG_n: each relay's table on the given leg; the backup table.
+share_tables() {
+  local i=0 leg
+  for leg in "$@"; do
+    share_leg_ok "$i" "$leg" || { echo "share_tables: $leg is not a leg of ${SH_NAME[$i]}" >&2; return 1; }
+    share_table_route "${SH_TABLE[$i]}" "$leg"
+    i=$((i + 1))
+  done
+  if [ -n "$SH_BK_IFACE" ]; then share_table_route "$SH_BK_TABLE" "$SH_BK_IFACE"; fi
+}
+# share_designate IFACE: table 102 and this host's routes to the tunnel prefixes.
+share_designate() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ip route replace default dev "$iface" table 102
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 102
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$iface" table 102
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 102
+  ip route replace 10.66.0.0/16 dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+}
+# share_map W_1 … W_n: the assignment map (ranges of jhash … mod 1000).
+share_map() {
+  local i=0 lo=0 w parts=""
+  for w in "$@"; do
+    if [ "$w" -gt 0 ]; then
+      parts="${parts:+$parts, }$lo-$((lo + w - 1)) : ${SH_VALUE[$i]}"
+      lo=$((lo + w))
+    fi
+    i=$((i + 1))
+  done
+  [ -n "$parts" ] || parts="0-999 : $SH_BK_VALUE"
+  echo "map { $parts }"
+}
+# share_apply UP DESIGNATED LEG_1 W_1 D_1 … LEG_n W_n D_n BACKUP_DRAIN
+# Checks every value against the compiled arrays (1: refused), then
+# changes the map, the redirect and drain rules in ONE nft batch (refused
+# whole or applied whole; 2: nft refused it, nothing changed), the relay
+# tables and table 102. Nothing else.
+share_apply() {
+  local up="$1" des="$2" n=${#SH_NAME[@]} i sum=0 leg w d bk map desif redirect="" drain="" v
+  shift 2
+  if [ $# -ne $((3 * n + 1)) ]; then echo "share_apply: wrong argument count" >&2; return 1; fi
+  local legs=() ws=() ds=()
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    leg="$1"; w="$2"; d="$3"; shift 3
+    share_leg_ok "$i" "$leg" || { echo "share_apply: $leg is not a leg of ${SH_NAME[$i]}" >&2; return 1; }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+MERIDIAN_NFT_BASE="$MERIDIAN_NFT"
+MERIDIAN_CHNROUTE_SAVED=/var/lib/meridian/lists/chnroute.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT_BASE" ] && [ -s "$MERIDIAN_CHNROUTE_SAVED" ]; then
+  if grep -qvE '^(flush set inet meridian chnroute6?|add element inet meridian chnroute6? \{ [0-9A-Fa-f.:/]+(, [0-9A-Fa-f.:/]+)* \})$' "$MERIDIAN_CHNROUTE_SAVED"; then
+    echo "meridian-chnroute-saved-ignored: $MERIDIAN_CHNROUTE_SAVED has unexpected lines; chnroute stays empty until the next list update" >&2
+  elif cat "$MERIDIAN_NFT_BASE" "$MERIDIAN_CHNROUTE_SAVED" > /var/lib/meridian/lists/.boot.nft; then
+    MERIDIAN_NFT=/var/lib/meridian/lists/.boot.nft
+    if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+      echo "meridian-chnroute-saved-ignored: the saved chnroute elements do not load with this ruleset; loading the compiled ruleset alone" >&2
+      MERIDIAN_NFT="$MERIDIAN_NFT_BASE"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft list table inet meridian_guard >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-guard-missing: inet meridian_guard is not loaded; refusing to enable forwarding" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+else
+  echo "meridian-nft-missing: $MERIDIAN_NFT not found; refusing to enable forwarding without the LAN guard" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if ! grep -q meridian-lists-derive-ready /usr/local/bin/meridian; then
+  echo "meridian-lists-derive-missing: /usr/local/bin/meridian has no lists-derive (run install.sh of this version)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if ! /usr/local/bin/meridian lists-derive; then
+  echo "meridian-lists-derive-failed: rule domain-sets not derived; forwarding not enabled" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+lan_if='eth0'
+lan_addr='192.168.77.2'
+ros4='192.168.77.1'
+lan_wait=${MERIDIAN_LAN_WAIT_SEC:-60}
+case "$lan_wait" in ''|*[!0-9]*) lan_wait=60 ;; esac
+lan_why=""
+lan_ready() {
+  local out
+  out=$(ip -o link show dev "$lan_if" 2>/dev/null) || { lan_why="interface $lan_if does not exist"; return 1; }
+  case "$out" in
+    *'<UP,'*|*',UP,'*|*',UP>'*|*'<UP>'*) ;;

+  esac

+    *" $lan_addr/"*) ;;

+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then

+#

+# the ULA drop and the fail-closed forward guard, that the loaded policy

+# behind it, that the guard's mark range is the compiled one, that the
+# foreign and domestic tables end in a blackhole, that the early-boot guard
+# file is the guard of the main ruleset, that the domestic lists the split
+# needs are not empty, that something listens on port 53, that the resolver
+# returns no AAAA for a tunnelled name while clients_ipv6_via_gateway is off
+# (a real query to 127.0.0.1), and — with
+# remote access on — that mra, its peers (public keys only), its guard
+# ingress, DNS, port, rules, routes and NAT are what was compiled; with it
+# off, that no mra exists. Every command's raw output is saved under the
+# evidence directory. INFO lines (list versions) are information, not checks;
+# WARN lines are risks the operator should act on and do not change the
+# exit status.

+# WebRTC tests need a browser on the test device; ICMP redirects and tunnel
+# cuts need a packet capture; remote access needs a real phone on a
+# cellular network and the router's port forward. Those are printed as

+# forwarding decision, source validation (rp_filter) included, for: a LAN
+# client to a domestic destination, a reply from each tunnel to a LAN
+# client and, with remote access on, a device to a domestic destination,
+# a domestic reply to a device and a tunnel reply to a device. An answer
+# such as "Invalid cross-device link" is a FAIL with the raw output kept.
