+# ip6_hex ADDR: the 32 hex digits of a plain IPv6 address (lower case, no
+# embedded IPv4); fails on anything else.
+ip6_hex() {
+  local a=$1 head tail g hex="" n i
+  local -a H=() T=()
+  case "$a" in ""|*[!0-9a-f:]*|*::*::*) return 1 ;; esac
+  case "$a" in
+    *::*)
+      head=${a%%::*} tail=${a#*::}
+      [ -z "$head" ] || IFS=: read -r -a H <<< "$head"
+      [ -z "$tail" ] || IFS=: read -r -a T <<< "$tail"
+      n=$((8 - ${#H[@]} - ${#T[@]}))
+      [ "$n" -ge 1 ] || return 1 ;;
+    *)
+      IFS=: read -r -a H <<< "$a"
+      n=0
+      [ "${#H[@]}" = 8 ] || return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  for g in ${H[@]+"${H[@]}"}; do
+    [ -n "$g" ] && [ ${#g} -le 4 ] || return 1
+    hex="$hex$(printf '%04x' "0x$g")"
+  done
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do hex="${hex}0000"; done
+  for g in ${T[@]+"${T[@]}"}; do
+    [ -n "$g" ] && [ ${#g} -le 4 ] || return 1
+    hex="$hex$(printf '%04x' "0x$g")"
+  done
+  printf '%s\n' "$hex"
+}
+# in_lan6_ula DST: DST (an address or prefix, as ip -6 route prints it) lies
+# inside the ULA LAN prefix. Always false when the LAN prefix is not a ULA.
+in_lan6_ula() {
+  local addr=${1%%/*} len=128 hex n r
+  [ -n "$lan6_ula" ] || return 1
+  case "$1" in */*) len=${1#*/} ;; esac
+  case "$len" in ""|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$len" -ge "$lan6_ula_bits" ] || return 1
+  hex=$(ip6_hex "$addr") || return 1
+  n=$((lan6_ula_bits / 4)) r=$((lan6_ula_bits % 4))
+  [ "${hex:0:n}" = "${lan6_ula_hex:0:n}" ] || return 1
+  [ "$r" = 0 ] && return 0
+  [ $((0x${hex:n:1} >> (4 - r))) = $((0x${lan6_ula_hex:n:1} >> (4 - r))) ]
+}
+# route_probe NAME DEV ARGS...: "ip ARGS" (a route lookup) with its raw
+# output kept as NAME.txt; succeeds only when the kernel resolved it to a
+# unicast route leaving on DEV. Otherwise probe_why says what it answered.
+route_probe() {
+  local first re=" dev $2( |\$)"
+  probe_why=""
+  run "$1" ip "${@:3}"
+  IFS= read -r first < "$evdir/$1.txt"
+  if [ "$rc" != 0 ]; then
+    case "$first" in
+      *"cross-device"*) probe_why="$first (source validation failed: a policy rule makes the kernel's reverse lookup fail)" ;;
+      exit=*) probe_why="ip exited $rc without output" ;;
+      *) probe_why="$first (ip exited $rc)" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  case "$first" in
+    exit=*) probe_why="no output" ;;
+    unreachable*|blackhole*|prohibit*|throw*|local*) probe_why="$first" ;;
+    *) [[ $first =~ $re ]] || probe_why="$first (not via $2)" ;;
+  esac
+  [ -z "$probe_why" ]
+}
+# probe_check ID WHAT DEV ARGS...: one route probe as a PASS or FAIL.
+probe_check() {
+  local id=$1 what=$2 dev=$3 n="rtget-$1"; shift 3
+  if route_probe "$n" "$dev" "$@"; then
+    pass "$id" "$what resolves out of $dev (ip $*)"
+  else
+    fail "$id" "$what: ip $* answered: $probe_why (evidence $n.txt)"
+  fi
+}
+# probe_tunnels ID WHAT DEV FAMILY DST SRC: a reply from every gateway tunnel
+# interface to DST must leave on DEV.
+probe_tunnels() {
+  local id=$1 what=$2 dev=$3 fam=$4 dst=$5 src=$6 tun bad="" n
+  for tun in $tun_ifaces; do
+    n="rtget-$id-$tun"
+    route_probe "$n" "$dev" "$fam" route get "$dst" from "$src" iif "$tun" || bad="$bad $tun: $probe_why (evidence $n.txt);"
+  done
+  if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
+    pass "$id" "$what from each tunnel ($tun_ifaces) resolves out of $dev"
+  else
+    fail "$id" "$what does not resolve out of $dev for:$bad"
+  fi
+}
+# out_of FILE: the command output without the exit= line run appends.
+out_of() { grep -v '^exit=[0-9]*$' "$1"; }
+# run NAME CMD...: raw output to $evdir/NAME.txt, exit status kept.
+run() {
+  name=$1; shift
+  "$@" > "$evdir/$name.txt" 2>&1
+  rc=$?
+  echo "exit=$rc" >> "$evdir/$name.txt"
+  return $rc
+}
+emit "meridian-verify $ts iface=$iface gateway=$gw_addr ros=$ros4 ros6=${ros6:-unset}"

+# --- kernel settings -------------------------------------------------------

+  # Policy rules as loaded: every compiled exit and region-group mark goes to

+    else

+  # The kernel's own decision for the paths that must forward.

+    if [ -n "$tun_ifaces" ]; then
+      probe_tunnels route_tunnel_reply6 "a reply from $foreign6 to the LAN client $lan_client6" "$iface" -6 "$lan_client6" "$foreign6"

+  fi

+  # Fallback: the foreign table (v4, v6) and the domestic table (v4) end in
+  # a blackhole, so a vanished tunnel or ROS route never falls through.

+    fi
+  else
+    fail fallback_blackholes "ip route show table 102/100 failed (evidence route4-102.txt route6-102.txt route4-100.txt)"
+  fi

+  # Remote access: present and wired when enabled, absent when not.
+  if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+    if run mra-link ip link show dev "$ra_if" && grep -qE '[<,]UP[,>]' "$evdir/mra-link.txt"; then

+      -4 route get "$ros4" from "$ra_dev4" iif "$ra_if" mark 0x64

+    if grep -q 'redirect to :53' "$m"; then pass dns_hijack_53 "LAN 53 is redirected to the local resolver"; else fail dns_hijack_53 "no 53 redirect in inet meridian"; fi
+    if grep -q 'redirect to :853' "$m"; then pass dns_hijack_853 "LAN 853 is redirected locally"; else fail dns_hijack_853 "no 853 redirect in inet meridian"; fi

+        grep -E 'dport [{] 53, 853 [}] ip saddr != ' "$m" | grep -qF "$ra_pool4" &&
+        grep -E 'dport [{] 53, 853 [}] ip6 saddr != ' "$m" | grep -qF "$ra_pool6"; then
+        pass remote_dns "53/853 from $ra_if is redirected locally and the DNS input allow-list holds $ra_pool4 and $ra_pool6"
+      else
+        fail remote_dns "the DNS hijack for $ra_if or the device pools in the DNS input allow-list are missing (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      fi
+      if grep -qE "iifname \"$iface\" udp dport $ra_port accept" "$m" && grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*udp dport $ra_port drop" "$m"; then
+        pass remote_port_lan_only "UDP $ra_port is accepted on $iface only"
+      else
+        fail remote_port_lan_only "the input rules accepting UDP $ra_port on $iface only are missing (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      fi
+      set -- $marks
+      n4=$(grep -F "ip saddr $ra_pool4 meta mark " "$m" | grep -cE ' snat (ip )?to ')
+      n6=$(grep -F "ip6 saddr $ra_pool6 meta mark " "$m" | grep -cE ' snat (ip6 )?to ')
+      if [ "$n4" -eq $# ] && [ "$n6" -eq $# ] && grep -qF "oifname \"$iface\" ip saddr $ra_pool4 masquerade" "$m" && grep -qF "oifname \"$iface\" ip6 saddr $ra_pool6 masquerade" "$m"; then
+        pass remote_nat "device pools have a transit SNAT for each of the $# marks and a masquerade on $iface"
+      else
+        fail remote_nat "device-pool NAT incomplete: $n4/$# v4 and $n6/$# v6 transit SNAT rules, masquerade on $iface required (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      fi
+    fi
+  else
+    fail nft_meridian "table inet meridian is not loaded (or not readable; run as root) (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- another loader that flushes the whole ruleset ------------------------
+# Without both Meridian tables, forwarded LAN traffic is unguarded: IPv4 and
+# IPv6 alike would leave via ROS (there is no routing-level backstop for
+# unmarked traffic). Debian's stock nftables.service loads
+# /etc/nftables.conf, which normally begins by flushing the whole ruleset;
+# whenever it runs after Meridian's tables are loaded (a restart or reload,
+# or a boot order that puts it later) it deletes them while forwarding is on.
+# This is a warning, not a check: whether and when it runs is the host's.
+if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && run nftables-service systemctl is-enabled nftables.service &&
+  [ "$(out_of "$evdir/nftables-service.txt")" = enabled ] &&
+  grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*flush[[:space:]]+ruleset' "$root/etc/nftables.conf" 2>/dev/null; then
+  warn nftables_service_flush "nftables.service is enabled and $root/etc/nftables.conf flushes the whole ruleset: if it runs after Meridian loaded its tables it deletes inet meridian and inet meridian_guard with forwarding on, and LAN IPv4 and IPv6 then leave via ROS unguarded. Disable it (systemctl disable nftables.service) or remove the flush (evidence nftables-service.txt)"
+fi
+
+# --- installed files: the early-boot guard is the main ruleset's guard -----
+if [ ! -f "$nftdir/meridian-guard.nft" ] || [ ! -f "$nftdir/meridian.nft" ]; then
+  fail guard_boot_file "$nftdir/meridian-guard.nft or meridian.nft is missing: meridian-guard.service has nothing to load at boot"
+elif bg=$(guard_block "$nftdir/meridian-guard.nft") && mg=$(guard_block "$nftdir/meridian.nft") && [ "$bg" = "$mg" ]; then
+  printf '%s\n' "$bg" > "$evdir/guard-boot-block.txt"
+  pass guard_boot_file "meridian-guard.nft holds exactly the guard of meridian.nft"
+else
+  printf '%s\n' "${bg:-}" > "$evdir/guard-boot-block.txt"
+  printf '%s\n' "${mg:-}" > "$evdir/guard-main-block.txt"
+  fail guard_boot_file "the early-boot guard differs from the guard in meridian.nft (evidence guard-boot-block.txt guard-main-block.txt)"
+fi
+
+# --- lists: versions are information; an empty domestic domain list fails --
+st="$listsdir/lists/status.json"
+if [ -f "$st" ] && run lists-status cat "$st"; then
+  in=0; name=""; src=""; cnt=""; upd=""; nlist=0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    if [ "$in" = 0 ]; then
+      [ "$l" = '  "published": {' ] && in=1
+      continue
+    fi
+    case "$l" in
+      '  }'*) in=0 ;;
+      '    "'*'": {') name=${l#    \"}; name=${name%\": \{}; src=""; cnt=""; upd="" ;;
+      '      "source": "'*) src=${l#*: \"}; src=${src%\",} ;;
+      '      "updated_at": "'*) upd=${l#*: \"}; upd=${upd%\",} ;;
+      '      "count": '*) cnt=${l#*: }; cnt=${cnt%,} ;;
+      '    }'*) info "list $name" "source=$src count=$cnt updated=$upd"; nlist=$((nlist + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done < "$st"
+  [ "$nlist" -gt 0 ] || info lists "status.json records no published list (evidence lists-status.txt)"
+else
+  info lists "no $st: no list update has run on this host since list sources were added"
+fi
+cn="$listsdir/geosite/cn.txt"
+if [ -f "$cn" ] && grep -qvE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$cn"; then
+  pass geosite_cn "$cn has domains (SmartDNS answers domestic names from domestic resolvers)"
+else
+  fail geosite_cn "$cn is missing or empty: domestic names are resolved abroad; run the list update (panel 名单 → 更新, or meridian-update-geosite.sh)"
+fi
+
+# --- DNS: something listens on 53 for the hijack to land on ----------------
+if ! command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  unknown dns_listener "ss not found; the port 53 listener was not checked"
+elif run ss-udp ss -H -lnu && run ss-tcp ss -H -lnt; then
+  if grep -qE ':53[[:space:]]' "$evdir/ss-udp.txt" && grep -qE ':53[[:space:]]' "$evdir/ss-tcp.txt"; then
+    pass dns_listener "a resolver listens on UDP and TCP 53 (whether it answers correctly is deploy/verify-smartdns.sh)"
+  else
+    fail dns_listener "nothing listens on UDP and TCP 53: the DNS hijack has no resolver behind it (evidence ss-udp.txt ss-tcp.txt)"
+  fi
+else
+  fail dns_listener "ss failed (evidence ss-udp.txt ss-tcp.txt)"
+fi
+
+# --- DNS: no AAAA for tunnelled names (docs/architecture.md「客户端 IPv6 与 AAAA」)
+# With clients_ipv6_via_gateway off the resolver answers AAAA for every name
+# that is not domestic with an empty NOERROR (force-AAAA-SOA): a phone that
+# takes IPv6 from the home router must not get an IPv6 address it would
+# reach over the home line, bypassing the tunnel. One real query for a
+# foreign name (MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME, default www.google.com; it must
+# not be in a domestic list) to the resolver on 127.0.0.1.
+aaaa_name=${MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME:-www.google.com}
+if [ "$clients_v6" = 1 ]; then
+  info dns_aaaa_tunnelled "clients_ipv6_via_gateway is on: AAAA is returned for exits and groups with egress_v6 (not checked here); it is only right if every client's IPv6 default route points at this gateway"
+elif [[ ! $aaaa_name =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?(\.[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)+$ ]]; then
+  fail dns_aaaa_tunnelled "MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME refused: only a host name"
+else
+  listed="" n=$aaaa_name
+  while [ -n "$n" ]; do
+    # The built-in domestic list as SmartDNS loads it (derived: names a
+    # rule matches are not in it; Apple is not built in any more).
+    f="$listsdir/geosite/ordered/gs_cn.txt"
+    [ -f "$f" ] && grep -qixF -e "$n" -e "-.$n" -e "*.$n" -- "$f" && listed="$n in $f"
+    case "$n" in *.*) n=${n#*.} ;; *) n="" ;; esac
+  done
+  if [ -n "$listed" ]; then
+    unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "the test name $aaaa_name is a domestic name ($listed); set MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME to a foreign name"
+  elif ! command -v dig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "dig not found (apt-get install bind9-dnsutils); the AAAA answer for a tunnelled name was not checked"
+  elif run dns-aaaa dig +time=3 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 AAAA "$aaaa_name"; then
+    if grep -qE '^[^;].*[[:space:]]IN[[:space:]]+AAAA[[:space:]]' "$evdir/dns-aaaa.txt"; then
+      fail dns_aaaa_tunnelled "the resolver returned AAAA for $aaaa_name although clients_ipv6_via_gateway is off: clients would reach it over the home line's IPv6, bypassing the tunnel (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+    elif grep -q 'status: NOERROR' "$evdir/dns-aaaa.txt"; then
+      pass dns_aaaa_tunnelled "AAAA for $aaaa_name is empty (NOERROR, no address): tunnelled names are IPv4-only while clients take IPv6 from the home router (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+    else
+      unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "the resolver did not answer AAAA $aaaa_name with NOERROR (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+    fi
+  else
+    unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "dig @127.0.0.1 AAAA $aaaa_name got no answer (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- DNS: domestic answers for unlisted names (unlisted_domestic_dns) -------
+# SmartDNS sends unlisted names to meridian-dns-split on 127.0.0.1:5356; it
+# accepts a domestic answer only when every address in it is in the China
+# lists it reads at start; empty lists accept nothing (every unlisted name
+# then gets the exit's answer, as with the setting off).
+if [ "$unlisted_dns" = 1 ]; then
+  if ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown dns_split_active "systemctl not found; meridian-dns-split.service was not checked"
+  elif run dns-split-active systemctl is-active meridian-dns-split.service; then
+    pass dns_split_active "meridian-dns-split.service is active (evidence dns-split-active.txt)"
+  else
+    fail dns_split_active "meridian-dns-split.service is not active: SmartDNS's only upstream for unlisted names is down, they get SERVFAIL (evidence dns-split-active.txt; journalctl -u meridian-dns-split)"
+  fi
+  bad=""
+  for f in "$listsdir/lists/china.txt" "$listsdir/lists/china6.txt"; do
+    if [ ! -f "$f" ] || ! grep -qvE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$f"; then
+      bad="$bad $f"
+    fi
+  done
+  if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
+    pass unlisted_domestic_lists "the China lists meridian-dns-split checks domestic answers against are present (an unlisted name gets the domestic answer only when every address in it is a China address)"
+  else
+    fail unlisted_domestic_lists "missing or empty:$bad — no domestic answer is accepted for unlisted names; run the list update (panel 名单 → 更新, or meridian-update-chnroute.sh)"
+  fi
+  info unlisted_domestic_dns "on: the domestic resolvers see every unlisted name, foreign ones included; those queries leave this gateway directly over the home line"
+fi
+
+# --- region-group DNS (docs/architecture.md「地区组的解析」) -----------------
+# Each group the hub switches is resolved at its own resolver address with
+# its own mark. What this host can show: the SNAT of its own marked queries
+# is loaded, SmartDNS's config asks each group's resolver with the mark in
+# decimal, and a marked lookup of each resolver address goes into a tunnel
+# (never the LAN port). Whether a member answers, and whether the answer
+# follows a failover, is only visible end to end (PENDING-HUMAN below).
+if [ -n "$grp_dns" ]; then
+  nm="$evdir/nft-meridian.txt"
+  if [ -f "$nm" ] && grep -qx 'exit=0' "$nm"; then
+    missing=""
+    while read -r lbl res mhex mdec transit dg; do
+      [ -n "$lbl" ] || continue
+      grep -F "ip6 daddr $res " "$nm" | grep -F "snat ip6 to $transit" | grep -qE "meta mark 0x0*${mhex#0x}( |\$)" || missing="$missing $lbl"
+    done <<< "$grp_dns"
+    if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
+      pass group_dns_snat "this host's marked queries to each group resolver are SNATed to the group's transit address"
+    else
+      fail group_dns_snat "no resolver SNAT loaded for group(s):$missing (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+    fi
+  else
+    fail group_dns_snat "table inet meridian could not be listed; the group resolver SNAT was not checked (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+  fi
+  conf="$root/etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf"
+  if [ ! -r "$conf" ]; then
+    unknown group_dns_upstream "$conf is not readable; the group resolver upstreams were not checked"
+  else
+    missing=""
+    while read -r lbl res mhex mdec transit dg; do
+      [ -n "$lbl" ] || continue
+      grep -E "^server $res -group $dg( |\$)" "$conf" | grep -qE " -set-mark $mdec( |\$)" || missing="$missing $lbl"
+    done <<< "$grp_dns"
+    if grep -qE '^server .*-set-mark 0[xX]' "$conf"; then
+      fail group_dns_upstream "$conf writes a -set-mark in hex: SmartDNS accepts it and applies no mark"
+    elif [ -z "$missing" ]; then
+      pass group_dns_upstream "$conf asks each group's resolver address with the group mark (decimal)"
+    else
+      fail group_dns_upstream "$conf has no marked resolver upstream for group(s):$missing"
+    fi
+  fi
+  if ! command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown group_dns_route "ip not found; the marked route to the group resolvers was not checked"
+  else
+    bad=""
+    while read -r lbl res mhex mdec transit dg; do
+      [ -n "$lbl" ] || continue
+      n="rtget-group-dns-$lbl"
+      run "$n" ip -6 route get "$res" mark "$mhex"
+      IFS= read -r first < "$evdir/$n.txt"
+      dev=""
+      [[ $first =~ \ dev\ ([^ ]+) ]] && dev=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
+      ok=0
+      if [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -n "$dev" ]; then
+        case "$first" in
+          unreachable*|blackhole*|prohibit*) ;;
+          *) case " $tun_ifaces " in *" $dev "*) ok=1 ;; esac ;;
+        esac
+      fi
+      [ "$ok" = 1 ] || bad="$bad $lbl: $first (evidence $n.txt);"
+    done <<< "$grp_dns"
+    if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
+      pass group_dns_route "a lookup of each group resolver address with the group mark resolves into a tunnel ($tun_ifaces), not $iface"
+    else
+      fail group_dns_route "a marked lookup of a group resolver address does not enter a tunnel:$bad"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- remote access: WireGuard state of mra (public keys only) --------------
+if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+  if ! command -v wg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    fail remote_wg "wg (wireguard-tools) is not installed: $ra_if cannot be configured"
+  else
+    if run mra-port wg show "$ra_if" listen-port && [ "$(out_of "$evdir/mra-port.txt")" = "$ra_port" ]; then
+      pass remote_listen "$ra_if listens on UDP $ra_port"
+    else
+      fail remote_listen "$ra_if does not listen on UDP $ra_port (evidence mra-port.txt)"
+    fi
+    if run mra-peers wg show "$ra_if" peers; then
+      missing=""; extra=0; npeer=0
+      while read -r k id; do
+        [ -n "$k" ] || continue
+        npeer=$((npeer + 1))
+        grep -qxF -- "$k" "$evdir/mra-peers.txt" || missing="$missing $id"
+      done <<< "$ra_peers"
+      while IFS= read -r k; do
+        case "$k" in ''|exit=*) continue ;; esac
+        case "$ra_peers" in "$k "*|*"
+$k "*) ;; *) extra=$((extra + 1)) ;; esac
+      done < "$evdir/mra-peers.txt"
+      if [ -z "$missing" ] && [ "$extra" = 0 ]; then
+        pass remote_peers "$ra_if has exactly the $npeer enabled devices as peers (public keys compared)"
+      else
+        fail remote_peers "$ra_if peers differ from the enabled devices:${missing:+ missing$missing;} $extra unexpected (evidence mra-peers.txt)"
+      fi
+    else
+      fail remote_peers "wg show $ra_if peers failed (evidence mra-peers.txt)"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- ROS fd00::/8 blackhole: only from a real read-only query --------------
+ros_ssh=${MERIDIAN_ROS_SSH:-}
+if [ -z "$ros_ssh" ]; then
+  pending ros_ula_blackhole "not executed. On ROS (read-only): /ipv6 route print where blackhole and (dst-address=fd00::/8 or dst-address=fc00::/7); archive the output, or rerun with MERIDIAN_ROS_SSH=user@$ros4"
+else
+  case "$ros_ssh" in
+    -*|*[!A-Za-z0-9@._:-]*)
+      fail ros_ula_blackhole "MERIDIAN_ROS_SSH refused: only user@host"
+      ;;
+    *)
+      if command -v ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 && run ros-ipv6-blackhole ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 -- "$ros_ssh" '/ipv6 route print terse where blackhole'; then
+        if grep -qE 'dst-address=(fd00::/8|fc00::/7)' "$evdir/ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt"; then
+          pass ros_ula_blackhole "ROS has a ULA blackhole (evidence ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt)"
+        else
+          fail ros_ula_blackhole "ROS answered but has no fd00::/8 or fc00::/7 blackhole (evidence ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt)"
+        fi
+      else
+        unknown ros_ula_blackhole "could not query ROS over ssh; nothing was checked (evidence ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt)"
+      fi
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+
+# --- not executable from this script ---------------------------------------
+if [ "$unlisted_dns" = 1 ]; then
+  pending dns_leak_client "dnsleaktest.com and ipleak.net on the test device (v4 and v6), plus a WAN capture with no 53/853 from the device itself; this script runs no browser. unlisted_domestic_dns is on: the leak sites list the domestic resolvers next to the exit's (their test names are unlisted, so this gateway asks the domestic resolvers too), and this gateway sends unlisted names, foreign ones included, to them over the home line; that is the expected result with the setting on, not a leak of the device"
+else
+  pending dns_leak_client "dnsleaktest.com and ipleak.net on the test device (v4 and v6), plus a WAN capture with no 53/853 from it; this script runs no browser"
+fi
+pending webrtc_srflx "browserleaks/ipleak WebRTC on the test device: srflx must be the exit address; a host GUA is a known limitation"
+pending redirect_on_wire "capture on the test device while browsing: no ICMP redirect from $gw_addr pointing at $ros4, and no ICMPv6 redirect from the gateway (Linux has no sysctl that stops IPv6 redirects)"
+pending tunnel_cut "take the exit tunnel down while the test device keeps browsing; capture on $iface: nothing foreign leaves towards $ros4, and the device gets no answer instead of a home-WAN answer"
+notrun netns_reload_no_leak "isolated Linux integration: sudo MERIDIAN_NETNS_TEST=1 go test ./internal/compile -run 'TestNetnsReloadNoLeak|TestNetnsULALANHomeAccess' (archive the log)"
+if [ -n "$grp_dns" ]; then
+  pending group_dns_failover "with a member of a switchable group stopped completely (tunnel and resolver): the hub moves the group, a new name of a group rule resolves and connects through the next member, and a capture on $iface shows no query to a domestic resolver or ROS for it (docs/verification.md)"
+  notrun netns_group_dns "isolated Linux integration: sudo MERIDIAN_NETNS_TEST=1 go test ./internal/compile -run TestNetnsGroupDNSFailover (members, the Mesh backup over an emulated overlay, refusal; archive the log)"
+fi
+notrun smartdns "sudo bash deploy/verify-smartdns.sh (archive the output)"
+notrun host_exec "sudo bash deploy/verify-host-exec.sh and --boot after a reboot (archive the output)"
+notrun mesh_veth "isolated Linux integration: sudo bash deploy/verify-mesh-veth.sh (dual-stack forwarding through the mmesh next-hops; archive the output). Mesh stays unverified until then"
+if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+  pending remote_phone_full "a real phone on cellular (Wi-Fi off) in full mode: handshake on UDP $ra_port, ipleak/dnsleaktest show the exit region and no carrier DNS, the panel and the other devices are unreachable (docs/remote-access.md)"
+  pending remote_phone_home "the same phone in home-only mode: LAN hosts and the gateway DNS answer; its other Internet traffic stays on the carrier and is not covered by Meridian"
+  pending remote_router_forward "the router forwards UDP $ra_port to $gw_addr; this script cannot see the router (show its NAT/port-forward rule read-only and archive it)"
+  pending remote_ipv6 "IPv6 inside the tunnel ($ra_pool6) and, if the endpoint has an AAAA record, dialing over IPv6 from a phone; neither is visible from here"
+fi
+
+emit "evidence: $evdir"
+if [ "$fails" -ne 0 ]; then
+  emit "meridian-verify-failed: $fails failed, $unknowns unknown"
+  exit 1
+fi
+if [ "$unknowns" -ne 0 ]; then
+  emit "meridian-verify-incomplete: $unknowns local checks could not run"
+  exit 2
+fi
+emit "meridian-verify-local-ok: local gateway checks passed. This is not a leak test; release still needs every PENDING-HUMAN and NOT-RUN-HERE item signed off with archived evidence."
+exit 0

+#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
+# Transit node. Does not NAT client traffic and does not own the default route.
+table inet meridian
+delete table inet meridian
+table inet meridian {
+  chain nested_snat {
+    type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept;
+    oifname "m06" ip saddr 10.66.200.22 rt ip nexthop 10.66.202.14 snat ip to 10.66.200.14 comment "group my on my1 (external exit on carrier dc2)"
+    oifname "m06" ip6 saddr fd66:0:0:ff::16 rt ip6 nexthop fd66::55:5 snat ip6 to fd66:0:0:ff::e
+    oifname "m05" ip saddr 10.66.200.24 rt ip nexthop 10.66.20.2 snat ip to 10.66.200.16 comment "group tw on tw2 (nested exit behind dc1)"
+    oifname "m05" ip6 saddr fd66:0:0:ff::18 rt ip6 nexthop fd66:0:0:14::2 snat ip6 to fd66:0:0:ff::10
+  }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Return path follows whichever west tunnel is actually up: IX, Aliyun WSS, then home WSS.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+IX=""
+ALI_WSS=""
+HOME_WSS="m04"
+IX_PEER=""
+ALI_PEER=""
+HOME_PEER="10.66.5.1"
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+GROUP_PLAN=6f9839296de3dfd6505b2112
+MESH_DEV=mmesh
+MESH_NH4=169.254.66.2
+MESH_NH6=fe80::66:2
+GROUP_TABLES="210 211 212 213 214 215 216"
+
+group_hop() {
+  local table="$1" dev="$2"
+  case "$table" in
+    ""|main|100|102|150)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  case " $GROUP_TABLES " in
+    *" $table "*) ;;
+    *)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table: not a region-group table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  [ -n "$dev" ] || return 1
+  local nh4="" nh6=""
+  case "$dev" in
+    *"|"*) nh4="${dev#*|}"; nh6="${nh4#*|}"; nh4="${nh4%%|*}"; dev="${dev%%|*}" ;;
+  esac
+  if [ "$dev" = "$MESH_DEV" ]; then
+    if ! ip link show "$MESH_DEV" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ ! -f /run/meridian/mesh-sealed ]; then
+      ip route replace blackhole default table "$table"
+      ip -6 route replace blackhole default table "$table"
+      echo "mmesh is not sealed; table $table stays blackholed" >&2
+      return 0
+    fi
+    # Ethernet veth: route via the sidecar's addresses, never "dev mmesh"
+    # alone (that would ARP/ND for every public destination).
+    ip route replace default via "$MESH_NH4" dev "$MESH_DEV" table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default via "$MESH_NH6" dev "$MESH_DEV" table "$table"
+  elif [ -n "$nh4" ] && [ -n "$nh6" ]; then
+    # A member behind another exit's tunnel (nested or external exit): the
+    # same device, told apart by next hop; the hub's nested_snat chain gives
+    # the group's packets that member's own transit source.
+    ip route replace default via "$nh4" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default via "$nh6" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+  else
+    ip route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+  fi
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+}
+
+group_can_return() {
+  local dir="$1" target="$2" now="$3" last="$4" st lo ok
+  st=$(cat "$dir/$target.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+  lo=$(cat "$dir/$target.lastok" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  ok=$(cat "$dir/$target.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  case "$ok" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$st" = "up" ] && [ "$lo" = "1" ] || return 1
+  [ $((now-ok)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ] || return 1
+  [ "$last" -eq 0 ] || [ $((now-last)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ]
+}
+group_step() {
+  local gid="$1" table="$2" target="$3" mesh="$4" hold="$5" manual="$6" treason="$7"
+  shift 7
+  local dir="/run/meridian/group/${gid}"
+  mkdir -p "$dir" /run/meridian/group-iface
+  local now id iface peer fails goods state okst lastok ids="" t_up=0 alt_id="" pairs=""
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  while [ $# -ge 3 ]; do
+    id="$1"; iface="$2"; peer="$3"; shift 3
+    ids="$ids $id"
+    pairs="$pairs $id=$iface"
+    echo "$iface" > "/run/meridian/group-iface/${id}"
+    fails=$(cat "$dir/$id.fails" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    goods=$(cat "$dir/$id.goods" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    state=$(cat "$dir/$id.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+    okst=$(cat "$dir/$id.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    case "$fails" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fails=0 ;; esac
+    case "$goods" in ''|*[!0-9]*) goods=0 ;; esac
+    [ "$state" = "down" ] || state=up
+    if alive "${iface%%|*}" "$peer"; then
+      lastok=1
+      [ -n "$okst" ] || okst="$now"
+      fails=0
+      if [ "$state" = "down" ]; then
+        goods=$((goods+1))
+        if [ "$goods" -ge "$RECOVERS_NEED" ]; then state=up; goods=0; fi
+      else
+        goods=0
+      fi
+    else
+      lastok=0; okst=""; goods=0
+      if [ "$state" = "up" ]; then
+        fails=$((fails+1))
+        if [ "$fails" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ]; then state=down; fails=0; fi
+      fi
+    fi
+    echo "$fails" > "$dir/$id.fails"
+    echo "$goods" > "$dir/$id.goods"
+    echo "$state" > "$dir/$id.state"
+    echo "$okst" > "$dir/$id.okst"
+    echo "$lastok" > "$dir/$id.lastok"
+    if [ "$id" = "$target" ] && [ "$state" = "up" ]; then t_up=1; fi
+    if [ "$id" != "$target" ] && [ "$state" = "up" ] && [ -z "$alt_id" ]; then alt_id="$id"; fi
+  done
+  local active want last ast dev reason hfail=""
+  active=$(cat "$dir/active" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  [ -n "$active" ] || active="$target"
+  if [ "$active" != "mmesh" ]; then
+    case " $ids " in *" $active "*) ;; *) active="$target" ;; esac
+  fi
+  last=$(cat "$dir/switched" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=0 ;; esac
+  want="$active"
+  if [ "$hold" = "1" ]; then
+    want="$target"
+  elif [ "$active" = "$target" ]; then
+    if [ "$t_up" -eq 0 ]; then
+      if [ -n "$alt_id" ]; then want="$alt_id"; elif [ "$mesh" = "1" ]; then want="mmesh"; fi
+    fi
+  elif group_can_return "$dir" "$target" "$now" "$last"; then
+    want="$target"
+  elif [ "$active" = "mmesh" ]; then
+    if [ -n "$alt_id" ]; then want="$alt_id"; fi
+  else
+    ast=$(cat "$dir/$active.state" 2>/dev/null || echo down)
+    if [ "$ast" != "up" ]; then
+      if [ -n "$alt_id" ]; then want="$alt_id"; elif [ "$mesh" = "1" ]; then want="mmesh"; fi
+    fi
+  fi
+  if [ "$want" != "$active" ]; then
+    if [ "$want" = "mmesh" ]; then dev="$MESH_DEV"; else dev=$(cat "/run/meridian/group-iface/$want" 2>/dev/null || true); fi
+    if group_hop "$table" "$dev"; then
+      active="$want"
+      echo "$active" > "$dir/active"
+      echo "$now" > "$dir/switched"
+    else
+      hfail="$want"
+    fi
+  elif [ "$active" = "mmesh" ]; then
+    # Staying on Mesh: re-apply every round, so the table follows the seal
+    # (via the sidecar while sealed, blackhole otherwise) and survives a
+    # re-created veth. Not a switch: active and switched stay as they are;
+    # the report reads the table (hop mmesh or blackhole).
+    group_hop "$table" "$MESH_DEV" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  if [ "$active" = "$target" ]; then
+    reason="$treason"
+    if [ "$t_up" -eq 0 ]; then
+      if [ "$hold" = "1" ]; then reason=held; fi
+      echo 1 > "$dir/alert"
+    else
+      echo 0 > "$dir/alert"
+    fi
+  elif [ "$active" = "mmesh" ]; then
+    reason=mesh; echo 1 > "$dir/alert"
+  elif [ "$manual" = "1" ]; then
+    reason=fallback; echo 1 > "$dir/alert"
+  else
+    reason=failover; echo 0 > "$dir/alert"
+  fi
+  [ -f "$dir/active" ] || echo "$active" > "$dir/active"
+  echo "$reason" > "$dir/reason"
+  group_record "$dir" "$gid" "$table" "$now" "$active" "$reason" "$hfail" "$pairs"
+}
+
+group_table_default() {
+  local fam="$1" table="$2" out line floor=0 i via
+  local -a w
+  out=$(ip "$fam" route show table "$table" 2>/dev/null) || { echo unreadable; return 0; }
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    read -r -a w <<< "$line"
+    [ "${#w[@]}" -gt 0 ] || continue
+    case " $line " in
+      *" metric 32767 "*)
+        [ "${w[0]}" = blackhole ] && floor=1
+        continue
+        ;;
+    esac
+    if [ "${w[0]}" = default ]; then
+      via=""
+      for ((i=1; i<${#w[@]}-1; i++)); do
+        if [ "${w[$i]}" = via ]; then via="${w[$((i+1))]}"; fi
+      done
+      for ((i=1; i<${#w[@]}-1; i++)); do
+        if [ "${w[$i]}" = dev ]; then
+          if [ -n "$via" ]; then echo "dev:${w[$((i+1))]}@$via"; else echo "dev:${w[$((i+1))]}"; fi
+          return 0
+        fi
+      done
+      echo other; return 0
+    fi
+    if [ "${w[1]:-}" = default ]; then
+      case "${w[0]}" in
+        blackhole) echo blackhole ;;
+        *) echo other ;;
+      esac
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done <<< "$out"
+  if [ "$floor" = 1 ]; then echo blackhole; else echo none; fi
+}
+group_table_hop() {
+  local a b
+  a=$(group_table_default -4 "$1")
+  b=$(group_table_default -6 "$1")
+  case "$a|$b" in
+    dev:*@*"|"dev:*@*)
+      if [ "${a%%@*}" = "${b%%@*}" ]; then echo "$a@${b#*@}"; return 0; fi
+      ;;
+  esac
+  if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then echo "$a"; else echo split; fi
+}
+group_record() {
+  local dir="$1" gid="$2" table="$3" now="$4" active="$5" reason="$6" hfail="$7" pairs="$8"
+  local tbl hop p h result=ok expect alert switched lastfail tmp
+  tbl=$(group_table_hop "$table")
+  case "$tbl" in
+    blackhole|none|split|unreadable|other) hop="$tbl" ;;
+    "dev:$MESH_DEV") hop=mmesh ;;
+    dev:*)
+      hop=other
+      for p in $pairs; do
+        h="${p#*=}"
+        if [ "dev:${h//|/@}" = "$tbl" ]; then hop="${p%%=*}"; break; fi
+      done
+      ;;
+    *) hop=unreadable ;;
+  esac
+  if [ -n "$hfail" ]; then
+    result=failed
+    echo "$hfail $now" > "$dir/hopfail.tmp" && mv -f "$dir/hopfail.tmp" "$dir/hopfail"
+  else
+    expect="$active"
+    if [ "$active" = "mmesh" ] && [ "$hop" = "blackhole" ]; then expect=blackhole; fi
+    [ "$hop" = "$expect" ] || result=diverged
+  fi
+  alert=$(cat "$dir/alert" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  case "$alert" in 1) ;; *) alert=0 ;; esac
+  switched=$(cat "$dir/switched" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  case "$switched" in ''|*[!0-9]*) switched=0 ;; esac
+  lastfail=$(cat "$dir/hopfail" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  tmp="$dir/.report.$$"
+  {
+    echo "meridian-group-report 1"
+    echo "group $gid"
+    echo "plan $GROUP_PLAN"
+    echo "beat $now"
+    echo "hop $hop"
+    echo "active $active"
+    echo "reason $reason"
+    echo "alert $alert"
+    echo "switched $switched"
+    echo "result $result"
+    if [ -n "$hfail" ]; then echo "want $hfail"; fi
+    if [ -n "$lastfail" ]; then echo "lastfail $lastfail"; fi
+    echo "end"
+  } > "$tmp" && mv -f "$tmp" "$dir/report" || rm -f "$tmp"
+  return 0
+}
+group_plan_record() {
+  local tmp="/run/meridian/.group-plan.$$"
+  mkdir -p /run/meridian
+  printf 'plan %s %s\n' "$GROUP_PLAN" "$(date +%s)" > "$tmp" && mv -f "$tmp" /run/meridian/group-plan
+}
+reset_groups() {
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/gb'
+  group_hop 210 'm07' || true
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/hk'
+  group_hop 211 'm05' || true
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/jp'
+  group_hop 212 'm08' || true
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/my'
+  group_hop 213 'm06|10.66.202.14|fd66::55:5' || true
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/sg'
+  group_hop 214 'm09' || true
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/tw'
+  group_hop 215 'm05|10.66.20.2|fd66:0:0:14::2' || true
+  rm -rf -- '/run/meridian/group/us'
+  group_hop 216 'm10' || true
+  group_plan_record || true
+  :
+}
+check_groups() {
+  group_step 'gb' 210 'gb1' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'gb1' 'm07' '10.66.8.2'
+  group_step 'hk' 211 'dc1' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'dc1' 'm05' '10.66.6.2' 'dc2' 'm06' '10.66.7.2'
+  group_step 'jp' 212 'jp1' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'jp1' 'm08' '10.66.9.2'
+  group_step 'my' 213 'my1' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'my1' 'm06|10.66.202.14|fd66::55:5' '10.66.202.14'
+  group_step 'sg' 214 'sg1' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'sg1' 'm09' '10.66.10.2'
+  group_step 'tw' 215 'tw2' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'tw2' 'm05|10.66.20.2|fd66:0:0:14::2' '10.66.20.2'
+  group_step 'us' 216 'us1' 0 0 1 'chosen' 'us1' 'm10' '10.66.11.2' 'us2' 'm11' '10.66.12.2'
+  :
+}
+
+alive() {
+  local iface="$1" peer="$2"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ping -I "$iface" -c 1 -W 2 -n "$peer" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+apply_west() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace blackhole "$LAN" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT4" metric 32767
+  ip route replace 10.66.0.0/16 dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT6" metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-9895c356
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m04 -o m05"
+  "-i m05 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m06"
+  "-i m06 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m07"
+  "-i m07 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m08"
+  "-i m08 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m09"
+  "-i m09 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m10"
+  "-i m10 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m11"
+  "-i m11 -o m04"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m04 m05 m06 m07 m08 m09 m10 m11; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit 'wstunnel-meridian.service'
+enable_unit meridian-failover.service
+systemctl restart meridian-failover.service
+echo meridian-up-complete

+#!/bin/bash
+# Return path follows whichever west tunnel is actually up: IX, Aliyun WSS, then home WSS.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+IX="m01"
+ALI_WSS=""
+HOME_WSS=""
+IX_PEER="10.66.2.1"
+ALI_PEER=""
+HOME_PEER=""
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+GROUP_PLAN=9ef2697b2f3b4364b2afad62
+MESH_DEV=mmesh
+MESH_NH4=169.254.66.2
+MESH_NH6=fe80::66:2
+GROUP_TABLES="210 211 212 213 214 215 216"
+
+group_hop() {
+  local table="$1" dev="$2"
+  case "$table" in
+    ""|main|100|102|150)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  case " $GROUP_TABLES " in
+    *" $table "*) ;;
+    *)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table: not a region-group table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  [ -n "$dev" ] || return 1
+  local nh4="" nh6=""
+  case "$dev" in
+    *"|"*) nh4="${dev#*|}"; nh6="${nh4#*|}"; nh4="${nh4%%|*}"; dev="${dev%%|*}" ;;
+  esac
+  if [ "$dev" = "$MESH_DEV" ]; then
+    if ! ip link show "$MESH_DEV" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ ! -f /run/meridian/mesh-sealed ]; then
+      ip route replace blackhole default table "$table"
+      ip -6 route replace blackhole default table "$table"
+      echo "mmesh is not sealed; table $table stays blackholed" >&2
+      return 0
+    fi
+    # Ethernet veth: route via the sidecar's addresses, never "dev mmesh"
+    # alone (that would ARP/ND for every public destination).
+    ip route replace default via "$MESH_NH4" dev "$MESH_DEV" table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default via "$MESH_NH6" dev "$MESH_DEV" table "$table"
+  elif [ -n "$nh4" ] && [ -n "$nh6" ]; then
+    # A member behind another exit's tunnel (nested or external exit): the
+    # same device, told apart by next hop; the hub's nested_snat chain gives
+    # the group's packets that member's own transit source.
+    ip route replace default via "$nh4" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default via "$nh6" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+  else
+    ip route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+  fi
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+}
+
+group_can_return() {
+  local dir="$1" target="$2" now="$3" last="$4" st lo ok
+  st=$(cat "$dir/$target.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+  lo=$(cat "$dir/$target.lastok" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  ok=$(cat "$dir/$target.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  case "$ok" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$st" = "up" ] && [ "$lo" = "1" ] || return 1
+  [ $((now-ok)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ] || return 1
+  [ "$last" -eq 0 ] || [ $((now-last)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ]

+group_step() {
+  local gid="$1" table="$2" target="$3" mesh="$4" hold="$5" manual="$6" treason="$7"
+  shift 7
+  local dir="/run/meridian/group/${gid}"
+  mkdir -p "$dir" /run/meridian/group-iface
+  local now id iface peer fails goods state okst lastok ids="" t_up=0 alt_id="" pairs=""
+  now=$(date +%s)

+    id="$1"; iface="$2"; peer="$3"; shift 3
+    ids="$ids $id"
+    pairs="$pairs $id=$iface"
+    echo "$iface" > "/run/meridian/group-iface/${id}"
+    fails=$(cat "$dir/$id.fails" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    goods=$(cat "$dir/$id.goods" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    state=$(cat "$dir/$id.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+    okst=$(cat "$dir/$id.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    case "$fails" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fails=0 ;; esac
+    case "$goods" in ''|*[!0-9]*) goods=0 ;; esac

+      lastok=1
+      [ -n "$okst" ] || okst="$now"
+      fails=0

+        goods=$((goods+1))

+      else
+        goods=0
+      fi
+    else
+      lastok=0; okst=""; goods=0
+      if [ "$state" = "up" ]; then
+        fails=$((fails+1))
+        if [ "$fails" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ]; then state=down; fails=0; fi
+      fi
+    fi
+    echo "$fails" > "$dir/$id.fails"
+    echo "$goods" > "$dir/$id.goods"
+    echo "$state" > "$dir/$id.state"
+    echo "$okst" > "$dir/$id.okst"
+    echo "$lastok" > "$dir/$id.lastok"

+    if [ "$id" != "$target" ] && [ "$state" = "up" ] && [ -z "$alt_id" ]; then alt_id="$id"; fi

+  case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=0 ;; esac

+    fi

+    if [ "$ast" != "up" ]; then
+      if [ -n "$alt_id" ]; then want="$alt_id"; elif [ "$mesh" = "1" ]; then want="mmesh"; fi
+    fi
+  fi
+  if [ "$want" != "$active" ]; then

+  elif [ "$active" = "mmesh" ]; then

+    # (via the sidecar while sealed, blackhole otherwise) and survives a
+    # re-created veth. Not a switch: active and switched stay as they are;
+    # the report reads the table (hop mmesh or blackhole).

+  fi

+    reason="$treason"
+    if [ "$t_up" -eq 0 ]; then
+      if [ "$hold" = "1" ]; then reason=held; fi
+      echo 1 > "$dir/alert"
+    else
+      echo 0 > "$dir/alert"
+    fi
+  elif [ "$active" = "mmesh" ]; then
+    reason=mesh; echo 1 > "$dir/alert"
+  elif [ "$manual" = "1" ]; then
+    reason=fallback; echo 1 > "$dir/alert"
+  else
+    reason=failover; echo 0 > "$dir/alert"
+  fi

+  echo "$reason" > "$dir/reason"

+group_table_default() {
+  local fam="$1" table="$2" out line floor=0 i via
+  local -a w
+  out=$(ip "$fam" route show table "$table" 2>/dev/null) || { echo unreadable; return 0; }

+    read -r -a w <<< "$line"
+    [ "${#w[@]}" -gt 0 ] || continue

+      *" metric 32767 "*)
+        [ "${w[0]}" = blackhole ] && floor=1
+        continue
+        ;;
+    esac
+    if [ "${w[0]}" = default ]; then
+      via=""
+      for ((i=1; i<${#w[@]}-1; i++)); do
+        if [ "${w[$i]}" = via ]; then via="${w[$((i+1))]}"; fi
+      done
+      for ((i=1; i<${#w[@]}-1; i++)); do
+        if [ "${w[$i]}" = dev ]; then
+          if [ -n "$via" ]; then echo "dev:${w[$((i+1))]}@$via"; else echo "dev:${w[$((i+1))]}"; fi
+          return 0
+        fi
+      done
+      echo other; return 0
+    fi
+    if [ "${w[1]:-}" = default ]; then
+      case "${w[0]}" in
+        blackhole) echo blackhole ;;
+        *) echo other ;;
+      esac
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done <<< "$out"
+  if [ "$floor" = 1 ]; then echo blackhole; else echo none; fi

+group_table_hop() {
+  local a b
+  a=$(group_table_default -4 "$1")
+  b=$(group_table_default -6 "$1")
+  case "$a|$b" in
+    dev:*@*"|"dev:*@*)
+      if [ "${a%%@*}" = "${b%%@*}" ]; then echo "$a@${b#*@}"; return 0; fi
+      ;;
+  esac
+  if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then echo "$a"; else echo split; fi

+group_record() {
+  local dir="$1" gid="$2" table="$3" now="$4" active="$5" reason="$6" hfail="$7" pairs="$8"
+  local tbl hop p h result=ok expect alert switched lastfail tmp
+  tbl=$(group_table_hop "$table")

+    blackhole|none|split|unreadable|other) hop="$tbl" ;;
+    "dev:$MESH_DEV") hop=mmesh ;;
+    dev:*)

+      for p in $pairs; do
+        h="${p#*=}"

+      done
+      ;;

+  esac

+    result=failed
+    echo "$hfail $now" > "$dir/hopfail.tmp" && mv -f "$dir/hopfail.tmp" "$dir/hopfail"

+    expect="$active"
+    if [ "$active" = "mmesh" ] && [ "$hop" = "blackhole" ]; then expect=blackhole; fi

+  fi
+  alert=$(cat "$dir/alert" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

+  switched=$(cat "$dir/switched" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  case "$switched" in ''|*[!0-9]*) switched=0 ;; esac
+  lastfail=$(cat "$dir/hopfail" 2>/dev/null || true)

+    echo "meridian-group-report 1"
+    echo "group $gid"
+    echo "plan $GROUP_PLAN"
+    echo "beat $now"
+    echo "hop $hop"
+    echo "active $active"
+    echo "reason $reason"
+    echo "alert $alert"
+    echo "switched $switched"
+    echo "result $result"
+    if [ -n "$hfail" ]; then echo "want $hfail"; fi
+    if [ -n "$lastfail" ]; then echo "lastfail $lastfail"; fi

+group_plan_record() {

+reset_groups() {

+  group_step 'jp' 212 'jp1' 1 0 0 'preferred' 'jp1' 'm15' '10.66.16.2'
+  group_step 'my' 213 'my1' 0 0 0 'preferred' 'my1' 'm13|10.66.202.14|fd66::55:5' '10.66.202.14'

+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767

+    if alive "$IX" "$IX_PEER"; then echo "$IX"; return; fi

+  if alive "$ALI_WSS" "$ALI_PEER"; then echo "$ALI_WSS"; return; fi
+  echo "$HOME_WSS"

+      bad=0
+    fi
+  else
+    bad=0
+  fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-d2c88527
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m00 -o m12"
+  "-i m12 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m13"
+  "-i m13 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m14"
+  "-i m14 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m15"
+  "-i m15 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m16"
+  "-i m16 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m17"
+  "-i m17 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m18"
+  "-i m18 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o mmesh"
+  "-i mmesh -o m00"
+  "-i m01 -o m12"
+  "-i m12 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m13"
+  "-i m13 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m14"
+  "-i m14 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m15"
+  "-i m15 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m16"
+  "-i m16 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m17"
+  "-i m17 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m18"
+  "-i m18 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o mmesh"
+  "-i mmesh -o m01"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Attach a veth to the Mesh sidecar netns and seal it.
+# Traffic the host injects on mmesh must not follow the container's default
+# route: that route is the docker bridge, which NATs onto this machine's WAN.
+# On the hub, that WAN is the VPS default route and would skip the exit.
+# The seal sends injected packets into table 170 (warp routes, or unreachable)
+# at priority 17000. It never installs a route in table 100, 102, 150, or main.
+#
+# mmesh is an Ethernet veth, not a point-to-point tunnel. Routes onto it
+# must name a next-hop: via 169.254.66.2 dev mmesh and via fe80::66:2 dev mmesh.
+# Both ends have fixed MACs and permanent neighbour entries, so no ARP/ND
+# is sent for public destinations and no proxy ARP/ND is needed.
+# The seal (/run/meridian/mesh-sealed) is only written when both next-hops
+# answer from the host.
+# This script refuses to run on the home gateway (192.168.100.88).
+set -u
+seal_only=0
+if [ "${1:-}" = "--seal-only" ]; then
+  seal_only=1
+fi
+unseal() {
+  rm -f /run/meridian/mesh-sealed
+}
+if ip -4 addr show 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'inet 192.168.100.88/'; then
+  echo "refusing to start mesh on the home gateway" >&2
+  unseal
+  exit 0
+fi
+if [ ! -s /etc/meridian/mesh.env ]; then
+  echo "mesh sidecar skipped: /etc/meridian/mesh.env is missing" >&2
+  unseal
+  exit 0
+fi
+if ! grep -q '^MESH_NODE_TOKEN=.\+' /etc/meridian/mesh.env; then
+  echo "mesh sidecar skipped: MESH_NODE_TOKEN is empty" >&2
+  unseal
+  exit 0
+fi
+compose=/etc/meridian/mesh-sidecar.compose.yml
+if [ ! -f "$compose" ]; then
+  echo "mesh compose missing" >&2
+  unseal
+  exit 0
+fi
+if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "docker is not installed; mesh sidecar not started" >&2
+  unseal
+  exit 0
+fi
+if [ "$seal_only" -eq 0 ]; then
+  docker compose -f "$compose" up -d || {
+    echo "mesh sidecar failed to start" >&2
+    unseal
+    exit 0
+  }
+fi
+cid=$(docker compose -f "$compose" ps -q mesh 2>/dev/null || true)
+pid=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' "$cid" 2>/dev/null || true)
+if [ -z "$pid" ] || [ "$pid" = "0" ]; then
+  echo "mesh sidecar is not running" >&2
+  unseal
+  exit 0
+fi
+if ip link show mmesh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if ! nsenter -t "$pid" -n ip link show mmesh-c >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    ip link del mmesh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+fi
+if ! ip link show mmesh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  ip link add mmesh address 02:6d:65:73:68:01 type veth peer name mmesh-c address 02:6d:65:73:68:02 || {
+    echo "mesh veth failed" >&2
+    unseal
+    exit 0
+  }
+fi
+ip link set mmesh address 02:6d:65:73:68:01 || true
+ip link set mmesh addrgenmode none >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.mmesh.disable_ipv6=0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.mmesh.accept_ra=0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+# meridian-ix-hub: ingress=198.51.100.10 iface=- egress=203.0.113.20
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m00 m01 m12 m13 m14 m15 m16 m17 m18; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-failover.service
+systemctl restart meridian-failover.service
+echo meridian-up-complete

===== nodes/jp1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-07da0276
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m08 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m08 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m15 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m15 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i mmesh -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o mmesh -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Attach a veth to the Mesh sidecar netns and seal it.
+# Traffic the host injects on mmesh must not follow the container's default
+# route: that route is the docker bridge, which NATs onto this machine's WAN.
+# On the hub, that WAN is the VPS default route and would skip the exit.
+# The seal sends injected packets into table 170 (warp routes, or unreachable)
+# at priority 17000. It never installs a route in table 100, 102, 150, or main.
+#
+# mmesh is an Ethernet veth, not a point-to-point tunnel. Routes onto it
+# must name a next-hop: via 169.254.66.2 dev mmesh and via fe80::66:2 dev mmesh.
+# Both ends have fixed MACs and permanent neighbour entries, so no ARP/ND
+# is sent for public destinations and no proxy ARP/ND is needed.
+# The seal (/run/meridian/mesh-sealed) is only written when both next-hops
+# answer from the host.
+# This script refuses to run on the home gateway (192.168.100.88).
+# Region-group resolver addresses this exit answers on mmesh. The panel's Mesh
+# deployment publishes each as a Cloudflare route of this exit's Mesh node:
+# meridian-mesh-publish fd66::53:c/128 group=jp
+set -u

+# every exit path of this script.

+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 171 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+    ip -6 route replace default via fe80::66:2 dev mmesh table 171 || echo "mesh DNS return route not installed; table 171 stays blackholed" >&2

+    ip -6 route del default via fe80::66:2 dev mmesh table 171 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi

===== nodes/sg1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-fb87aa3c
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m09 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m09 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m16 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m16 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc
