+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='sg1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m09 m16; do

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-1b224e02
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m19 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m19 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='tw2'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"

+    exit 1

===== nodes/us1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-07354b30
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m10 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m10 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m17 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m17 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='us1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4,6
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m10 m17; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-unlock.timer
+if [ -f /etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if systemctl cat meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    systemctl restart meridian-smartdns.service || echo "meridian-smartdns.service restart failed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi
+echo meridian-up-complete

===== nodes/us2/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-d85e7dc1
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m11 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m11 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m18 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m18 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='us2'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"
 
===== nodes/us2/usr/local/sbin/meridian-up.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+for iface in m11 m18; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-unlock.timer
+if [ -f /etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if systemctl cat meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    systemctl restart meridian-smartdns.service || echo "meridian-smartdns.service restart failed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi
+echo meridian-up-complete
+
